observation: SessionStore::create() generates a new active session directory whenever the preferred id already exists; it does not enforce one active session per task. WorkflowPlanCommand already rejects multiple active sessions, but WorkflowStartCommand previously called create() unconditionally. Retrying workflow start after a recall failure could therefore create a second active session and make later approve/close resolution ambiguous.

evidence.reference: PR #28 CodeRabbit review thread PRRT_kwDOTALgUs6XZVxl: repeated workflow start can create multiple active sessions

evidence.command: pending: WorkflowStartCommand retry and multi-active tests
evidence.summary: Validation is pending. Promote only if restart reuses the existing active session, an already-corrupt multi-active state fails before recall compilation, and the complete CI/self-shape/release-set matrix remains green.

hypothesis: Every workflow entrypoint that creates or resumes session state must preserve the same one-active-session-per-task invariant; retries should reuse the active session rather than allocate a new one.
